titulo: The present subjunctive: forms: What the subjunctive is and how to build it

aula.objetivo: Understand the subjunctive as the mood for what is not (yet) a fact, and form the present subjunctive of regular verbs, of verbs with irregular «eu» forms and of the twelve key irregulars: ser, estar, ter, ir, fazer, ver, vir, dar, saber, querer, poder, haver.

sessao.titulo: What the subjunctive is and how to build it

blocos.titulo: The subjunctive: a mood for what is not a fact
blocos.explicacao: STEP 1: verbs have moods. The indicative is the mood of facts and certainties: «Ele chega às nove», «Eu sei que você mora aqui». The subjunctive (o subjuntivo) is the mood of what is not a fact: a wish, a doubt, an emotion, a plan, a condition. Compare «Ele vem» (fact) and «Espero que ele venha» (wish). STEP 2: you hear it almost always after the word «que», or after words like «talvez» (maybe) and «tomara que» (hopefully). The verb before it, such as «esperar», «querer» or «duvidar», tells you that what follows is not a fact. STEP 3: how to form the present subjunctive of any regular verb. Take the «eu» form of the present, drop the final -o and add the «opposite vowel» endings. Verbs in -ar take an «e»: -e, -es, -e, -emos, -em. Verbs in -er and -ir take an «a»: -a, -as, -a, -amos, -am. Example: falo, «fal-» + «e» gives «fale»; como, «com-» + «a» gives «coma»; parto, «part-» + «a» gives «parta». STEP 4: this is why the verbs that are irregular in the «eu» form carry the irregularity into every person: «faço» gives «faça», «tenho» gives «tenha», «venho» gives «venha», «vejo» gives «veja», «digo» gives «diga», «saio» gives «saia». STEP 5: «você», «ele», «ela» and «a gente» use the same form as «eu». You already know these forms: the imperative of lesson 28 («fale», «venha», «faça») is the subjunctive.
blocos.comparacao: English has almost lost the subjunctive: only traces remain, as in «I suggest that he go», «It is important that she be here» and «If I were you». Portuguese keeps it alive and uses it every day. The good news: you do not translate it word by word; you learn the triggers (wish, doubt, emotion, plan, condition) that tell you to switch from the indicative to the subjunctive.

exemplos.ru: Espero que ele chegue às nove.
exemplos.pt: I hope he arrives at nine. (wish)
I doubt that you live here. (doubt)

erros.motivo: After «esperar que» the verb is in the subjunctive: the arrival is a wish, not a fact.
For -ar verbs the subjunctive ending is -e, not -a or -as.
For -er and -ir verbs the subjunctive ending is -a: the vowels swap.

blocos.enunciado: Say five facts with the indicative («Eu falo português», «Ela mora aqui»), then turn each one into a doubt or a wish using «duvido que…» or «espero que…» and the subjunctive.
Say the present (eu form) of these verbs: falar, comer, partir, fazer, ter, vir, ver, dizer, sair, pedir. You will need the «eu» form today: it is the starting point of the subjunctive.
